easy.def: Something you know or have seen before.
examples: That song is familiar. I know it!
I saw a familiar face at the store.
This street looks familiar.

more.def: Known to you because you have seen, heard, or done it before.
examples: His voice sounded familiar, but I could not remember his name.
The smell of baking bread was familiar and comforting.
Are you familiar with the rules of this game?
She is a famous singer.
The famous writer came to our school.
This city is famous for its bridge.

more.def: Known and recognized by very many people.
examples: The famous painting hangs in a museum in Paris.
The town is famous for its delicious cheese.
He became famous after he climbed the tall mountain.
Blue is my favorite color.
This is my favorite bear.
What is your favorite food?

more.def: Liked more than all the others.
examples: My favorite part of the book is the surprise ending.
Her favorite subject in school is science.
We went to our favorite park for the picnic.

easy.def: A big party for a special day.
examples: We ate treats at the festival.
There was music at the festival.
We go to the fall festival.

more.def: A special time when people celebrate with events, food, or music.
examples: The town holds a kite festival every spring.
The film festival shows movies from around the world.
Lanterns lit up the streets during the festival.
The tiger looks fierce.
A fierce dog barked at us.
The storm was fierce.

more.def: Wild, strong, and ready to attack; or very strong and powerful.
examples: A fierce wind bent the trees almost to the ground.
The fierce lion roared to protect her cubs.
The two teams were in a fierce battle for first place.
A rubber band is flexible.
The straw is flexible.
A cat's body is flexible.

more.def: Able to bend easily without breaking; or able to change easily.
examples: Gymnasts stretch every day to stay flexible.
The flexible branch bent but did not snap.
Our plans are flexible, so we can go on either day.

easy.def: To stay on top of water or in the air.
examples: My toy boat can float.
A cloud floats in the sky.
I can float on my back.

more.def: To rest on top of a liquid or drift gently through the air.
examples: A leaf floated slowly down the stream.
The balloon floated up over the rooftops.
Ice floats because it is lighter than water.

easy.def: A big place with lots of trees.
examples: Deer live in the forest.
An owl hooted in the forest.
We camp in the forest.

more.def: A large area of land covered with trees and other plants.
examples: We followed a narrow trail through the forest.
The forest floor was covered with fallen leaves.
Many animals lost their homes when the forest burned.

easy.def: A very old bone or mark from a plant or animal, found in rock.
examples: We saw a dinosaur fossil.
I found a fossil of a shell.
The fossil is in a rock.

more.def: What is left of a plant or animal from long ago, kept safe in rock.
examples: The fossil showed the shape of a fish that lived millions of years ago.
Fossils help scientists learn about animals from long ago.
He found a leaf fossil in a piece of stone.
An egg is fragile. Do not drop it!
The fragile cup broke.
Baby birds are fragile.

more.def: Easily broken, so it must be handled with care.
examples: The box was marked "fragile" because it held glass cups.
The old book's pages were thin and fragile.
Carry the model carefully because it is fragile.

easy.def: Being able to do and say what you want.
examples: The bird flew away to freedom.
The dog loves the freedom of the big yard.
We have the freedom to pick our own books.

more.def: The right to act, speak, and think as you choose.
examples: The people fought for their freedom.
Summer vacation gives kids the freedom to play all day.
The zoo released the healed eagle back to freedom.
Loud noises frighten my cat.
The big dog frightened the baby.
Spiders do not frighten me.
The sudden bang frightened the horses.
The scary movie frightened my little brother.
A sudden shadow frightened the fish away.
Dad was furious when the dog ate the cake.
The furious bee buzzed at us.
Mom was furious about the mud on the rug.
She was furious when she found out someone had broken her model.
The coach was furious when the team skipped practice.
He was furious with himself for losing his new jacket.

easy.def: The time that has not come yet.
examples: In the future, I want to be a vet.
We will have a new school in the future.
No one can see the future.

more.def: The time that is still to come, after now.
examples: No one knows exactly what will happen in the future.
In the future, cars may drive themselves.
She is saving her money for the future.
